_note: Brake pads for Track sessions (the Add page's Brake pads drop-downs, Compare pads on the leaderboard). Makes with their compounds, and for each compound what its maker publishes: its intended use, its friction level (mu) and its working temperature range in degrees C. Leave a figure out rather than guess it. Edit them on the Brake pads panel of track-admin.html, which stores its changes on top of this file. Each compound's source is the page its figures came from.

compounds.name: XP8
compounds.notes: High torque, good initial bite at race temperatures, very high fade resistance, kind to discs; maker says ideal for track days

compounds.name: XP10
compounds.notes: Very strong initial bite and high friction, very kind to discs

compounds.name: XP12
compounds.notes: More bite, torque and fade resistance than XP10, good release and modulation; harder on discs than XP10

compounds.name: XP20
compounds.notes: Extremely aggressive initial bite, linear torque curve and excellent fade resistance; maker says not for street use
High performance street compound with good release, low dust and low noise; maker says not recommended for any track use; range starts at ambient and tops out at 426C+

compounds.name: Greenstuff
compounds.notes: Street pad with more friction and fade resistance than standard, ECE R90 approved

compounds.name: Redstuff
compounds.notes: Copper-free ceramic sport pad, very low dust and long life; a road pad, not for track use

compounds.name: Yellowstuff
compounds.notes: High friction fast road pad; long bedding-in, so EBC does not recommend it for track use

compounds.name: Bluestuff
compounds.notes: Figures for Bluestuff NDX; track day and sprint pad with road manners, short bedding-in

compounds.name: Ultimax2
compounds.notes: R90 approved replacement pad for daily driving; maker says not suitable for track use

compounds.name: ME20
compounds.notes: Semi-metallic sprint race pad, stable when hot, low wear

compounds.name: MX72
compounds.notes: Ceramic carbon metal pad for fast driving and circuit use, works from low temperatures

compounds.name: DS2500
compounds.notes: For track days, light race use and the rear axle on GT cars

compounds.name: DS1.11
compounds.notes: Heavy duty endurance pad, long life and very kind to discs

compounds.name: DS3.12
compounds.notes: High friction and initial bite; GT and heavy duty use, sprint and medium length races

compounds.name: DSUNO
compounds.notes: Heavy duty semi-endurance pad, very controllable, kind to discs, long life

compounds.name: DS3000
compounds.notes: Competition compound for touring cars, rally, formula and track cars with OE brakes; maker says not suitable for road use

compounds.name: DS Performance
compounds.notes: Road pad with a racing feel and ECE R90 approval; 0.46 is the average from a fast-road test schedule and would be lower for race use

compounds.name: HP+
compounds.notes: Crossover road and race pad for low to mid temperatures, smooth torque

compounds.name: DTC-60
compounds.notes: For very high deceleration, good release and torque control, low disc wear

compounds.name: DTC-70
compounds.notes: Very high torque and aggressive initial bite, good modulation and release

compounds.name: HPS
compounds.notes: Fahrenheit figures converted to Celsius, rounded to the nearest 5. Street compound for street-legal cars, excellent for spirited driving; optimal range 100-500 F

compounds.name: HPS 5.0
compounds.notes: Fahrenheit figures converted to Celsius, rounded to the nearest 5. Ferro-Carbon street compound with aggressive torque; optimal range 100-550 F

compounds.name: DTC-30
compounds.notes: Fahrenheit figures converted to Celsius, rounded to the nearest 5. Controllable-torque multi-purpose race compound for circle track, drag racing and similar; optimal range 100-800 F

compounds.name: DTC-80
compounds.notes: Fahrenheit figures converted to Celsius, rounded to the nearest 5. High torque, high temperature race compound for circle track and road racing; optimal range 600-1500 F

compounds.name: Blue 9012
compounds.notes: Fahrenheit figures converted to Celsius, rounded to the nearest 5. Entry level endurance race compound, medium torque, easy to bed in; optimal range 350-800 F

compounds.name: Performance Ceramic
compounds.notes: Fahrenheit figures converted to Celsius, rounded to the nearest 5. Low noise, ultra-low dust street pad; optimal range 100-450 F

compounds.name: M1144
compounds.notes: Medium torque, excellent low temperature performance; track days, hill climbs and club motorsport

compounds.name: M1155
compounds.notes: Track and rally pad, medium friction, positive modulation and high fade resistance

compounds.name: M1166
compounds.notes: High-torque racing compound with strong fade resistance and stability at high temperature; nominal mu 0.46 per maker spec sheet; maker lists track days among typical uses

compounds.name: RS29
compounds.notes: Classic yellow compound, now sold as RSL 29

compounds.name: RSL19
compounds.notes: Low metallic, medium friction, stable over a broad range; GT3 rear or lighter GT and touring car front

compounds.name: RSL29
compounds.notes: Low metallic, medium friction, very good modulation and release; club racing, track days and GT endurance

compounds.name: RSL1
compounds.notes: Very high heat resistance, constant friction over a wide temperature range, low wear; maker says used in GT, touring and prototype endurance racing and often in sprint races

compounds.name: ProTrack
compounds.notes: Ceramic metallic compound with milder initial bite than ProRace; maker says suited to light, occasional track use or wet conditions and low grip tyres

compounds.name: ProRace
compounds.notes: Ceramic graphite compound with great initial bite and control; maker says used in many race series and the compound of choice for many track day users

compounds.name: ProComp S2
compounds.notes: High metallic content; maker says it has the highest friction rating of the ProComp range

compounds.name: ProComp E1
compounds.notes: High metallic content; maker says it suits endurance race applications and club enduro series and has the best wear rate of the ProComp range, with good modulation

compounds.name: ProComp E2
compounds.notes: High metallic content; maker says it has a higher friction rating than the E1 with a low wear rate

compounds.name: ProComp R
compounds.notes: Made for rear applications with lower bite and torque, smooth release, works with ABS, low wear rates

compounds.name: ProComp S1
compounds.notes: High metallic content; maker says suitable for sprint, race and rally, with the best lower temperature performance in the ProComp range, high bite and good modulation
Endurance pad for high temperatures, smooth bite, very long wearing, low disc wear
Sprint and medium distance pad: smooth bite, friction rising with temperature, good release
Maker calls it a race compound with good initial bite and very little torque rise with temperature; sprint or medium distance; used in touring car, TCR, NASCAR, formula, rally and trackday
Slight friction rise with temperature, excellent release and modulation, very low disc wear and the longest pad wear of all PFC pads; maker says replaced by 08 compound in many pad shapes

compounds.name: R6
compounds.notes: Autocross compound with ultra-high cold torque from dead cold; maker does not recommend it for road racing (closed circuit) in most applications; maker does not say whether the range is rotor or pad temperature

compounds.name: R8
compounds.notes: High torque with good initial bite and extremely high fade resistance, kind to rotors; maker says perfect for track day use and not recommended for daily street use; maker does not say whether the range is rotor or pad temperature

compounds.name: R10
compounds.notes: Stronger initial bite and higher friction than R8, leads the industry in rotor friendliness per the maker; not recommended for daily street use; maker does not say whether the range is rotor or pad temperature

compounds.name: R12
compounds.notes: Excellent initial bite, high consistent torque and outstanding fade resistance over R10, slightly more rotor aggressive than R10; not recommended for daily street use; maker does not say whether the range is rotor or pad temperature

compounds.name: R4-S
compounds.notes: Maker says for high performance and heavy duty street use, rotor friendly with low dust and squeal, and not recommended for track use; no friction or temperature figures published

compounds.name: R4-E
compounds.notes: Carbon Kevlar full race compound that lasts longer than R-4 and suits club enduro events; maker says it performs best averaging over 600°F, converted to 315°C and rounded to the nearest 5; maker does not say whether this is pad or rotor temperature and gives no upper limit

compounds.name: Club Racer
compounds.notes: Export-only RC09 pad designed for circuit driving, circuit use only; maker's range is the applicable rotor temperature

compounds.name: Type PS
compounds.notes: Affordable non-steel pad for dependable braking and improved anti-fade in sport driving; maker's range is the applicable rotor temperature

compounds.name: Type HC+
compounds.notes: Superior braking and control across a wide temperature range; maker's range is the applicable rotor temperature

compounds.name: Racing 777
compounds.notes: Maker says full braking effect and sturdy wear resistance, ideal for sprints to semi-endurance races, circuit use only; maker's range is the applicable rotor temperature

compounds.name: Racing N+
compounds.notes: Linear braking and stable control in extreme circuit driving, circuit use only and for certain vehicle models only; maker's range is the applicable rotor temperature

compounds.name: BP-10
compounds.notes: BP series compound, not PolyMatrix; low-medium temperature and friction, light dusting and quiet, aimed at spirited street use; no figures published

compounds.name: BP-20
compounds.notes: BP series compound, not PolyMatrix; med-high temperature and friction, dual-sport pad for street with expanded range for autocross and track events; no figures published

compounds.name: PolyMatrix B
compounds.notes: High temperature and friction, consistent response after minimal warm-up, used in oval, road course and off-road competition; no figures published

compounds.name: PolyMatrix E
compounds.notes: Medium temperature and friction mid-level race compound with linear response, for autocross, rally, fast drag and off-road; page does not call it BP-28; no figures published

compounds.name: W3
compounds.notes: Low steel, high performance street and sprint race, the most versatile pad; maker gives the range as NT to 650°C (NT presumably normal temperature, so no minimum set) and does not say rotor or pad

compounds.name: W4
compounds.notes: Low steel pad for sprint racing with superb control and excellent torque control; maker does not say rotor or pad temperature

compounds.name: W5
compounds.notes: High steel pad for club racing, a balance of effectiveness and braking control; maker does not say rotor or pad temperature
